If colors are indistinguishable due to small error tolerance, use an alternate error metric: the difference between parent and child error values, excluding the maximum error value of the child nodes [S1].

The claim states that if colors are indistinguishable due to small error tolerance, an alternate error metric should be used: the difference between parent and child error values, excluding the maximum error value of the child nodes. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Specifying a small error tolerance to decide the LOD could result in getting nodes with rather similar error values, which means that the treemap may end up with showing some indistinguishable colors. In this case, we can use an alternate error metric... it does not include the maximum error value of the child nodes and only shows the difference between the parent and the child nodes.' This matches the claim exactly.
